🧠 Crypto News Brief: Crypto shrugged off the midterm shock: Bitcoin reclaimed $80K on a short squeeze and returning ETF inflows, even as a Democratic Congress dims the CLARITY Act's odds and Binance-hack fallout keeps regulators focused on security. 📈 Bitcoin Reclaims $80K as Shorts Get Squeezed Bitcoin climbed back above $80,000 after briefly sliding toward $75,600 as U.S. midterm results came in. Roughly $378 million in bearish bets were liquidated within an hour, while spot BTC ETFs logged $74.6M in net inflows on Nov. 4, snapping a three-day outflow streak worth about $1.16B. Traders now eye resistance near $81,300–$82,000. Read full story 🏦 Fed and OCC Check Bank Defenses After Binance Hack Federal Reserve and OCC supervisors began calling U.S. banks to ask about vulnerabilities, unusual activity or service disruptions following last week's record $6.3 billion Binance heist, Reuters reported citing sources. One major bank's cybersecurity team is drafting an internal review, and sources flagged fast-evolving AI as a key challenge. Both regulators declined to comment. More details 🗳️ Democratic Sweep Puts the CLARITY Act on Life Support Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate, further dimming prospects for the CLARITY Act, the market-structure bill that already failed to advance in September under Republican control. Industry voices told CoinDesk the bill is likely dead in its current form. The new Congress is seated Jan. 3, 2027, while the SEC and CFTC can keep writing rules under existing authority. Read more 🔀 Trump Media Moves $342M in Bitcoin to Crypto.com Wallets attributed to Trump Media & Technology Group sent about 4,259 BTC — roughly $342 million — to Crypto.com, according to Arkham data. On-chain moves do not prove a sale, and the company described earlier transfers as custody or trading management. The amount nearly matches BTC pledged as convertible-note collateral ahead of a Nov. 30 noteholder repayment date. See details 🇭🇰 Hong Kong Passes Crypto Tax Reporting Law Hong Kong adopted the OECD's Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework into law. From 2027, exchanges and other covered providers must collect customer identities, tax residency and records of purchases, sales, crypto-to-crypto swaps and transfers to external wallets, with data shared with overseas tax authorities from 2028. **BTC** $80,048 (2.3%) | **ETH** $2,409 (3.9%) | **SOL** $96 (3.2%)

* South Korea delays its crypto tax until 2029, the [fourth postponement](https://www.chooserich.live/story/south-korea-delay-crypto-tax-jsf53t8)

* Coinbase says Binance's hot wallet incident had [no impact](https://www.chooserich.live/story/coinbase-unaffected-binance-wallet-incident-rukneuh) on its platform

* Trump-backed American Bitcoin reports [Q3 profit](https://www.chooserich.live/story/american-bitcoin-q3-profit-8sefsv8) after three straight quarterly losses

* Fed and OCC check bank systems for fallout after the [Binance hack](https://www.chooserich.live/story/us-regulators-banks-binance-hack-7vmaw3z)

* Bitcoin rebounds to about [$78,055](https://www.chooserich.live/story/bitcoin-ethereum-slide-midterm-elections-yqry63h), erasing losses

81997.body:
PFI Monthly 

Автор: Prague Finance Institute


Автор: Prague Finance Institute

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/pfi-monthly-october-edition-prague-finance-institute-wawpf?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BLhpsf2MiSYq8JGsKrChLDg%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=2d_waybYpadsw1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mw3hqz6f~q9-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mw3hqz6f-q9
  
Dear professionals, We are pleased to share the October edition of the PFI Monthly Research Report. This issue explores key themes shaping global macro and currency markets, central banking, the AI investment cycle and its financing, equity valuations, Czech healthcare financing, M&A, private equity and behavioral finance. In this issue of PFI Monthly you will find: Interview – Petr Zabza of Air Bank on behavioral resilience as the core of financial literacy, why AI is not a bubble as a technology but parts of its pricing look like one, whether multi-decade-high bond yields are an entry point, and where the risks sit in Czech corporate bonds. Global markets dashboard – the month in numbers as of 30 October 2026: currencies, government and corporate bond yields, regional equities, sectors and commodities. Global macro – Japan’s Ministry of Finance has sold roughly $175bn of dollar reserves this year. Why the structural flows that weakened the yen have reversed, and why the asymmetry may now run against the shorts. Plus the 2026 Nobel Prize in Economics for Robert Hall and Michael Woodford, and what it means for central banks and markets, with the Fed under Kevin Warsh moving away from forward guidance. Central banking – A critical look at Governor Michl’s three arguments for a “harder, better, faster, stronger” CNB: inflation, gold reserves and public trust. Financial markets – The S&P 500 gained 14.8% a year after the 2009 low. A decomposition into revenues, margins and valuation shows why the next decade may look very different. Further pieces cover the cracks in the AI boom (negative free cash flow at big tech, Intel’s sell-off, CoreWeave’s credit stress), the moment AI demand met the cost of capital, and how competing index rules will decide who buys Anthropic after its S-1 filing. Corporate finance – Czech ambulatory care is being consolidated by a handful of domestic holdings, funded increasingly by bonds. A look at who owns what, how it is paid for and why the real risk sits with the public payer. Czech M&A – Pegasus Airlines completes its acquisition of Czech Airlines and Smartwings Group: deal terms, antitrust remedy and the background to the transaction. Private equity – Recurring revenue no longer justifies a premium on its own. What software buyers and lenders now test before they pay: proprietary data, workflo
